title: Image Captioning · Observability
description: Top→bottom: health, throughput, latency, payload & pipeline, hardware, correlation, metadata. Palette: Okabe-Ito (colour-blind safe); markers + dash styles distinguish series without colour.

options.content: **The story:** all tiles should be blue. If the app or node exporter turns orange-red, nothing below can be trusted. “No data” on Success ratio or Last request only means no traffic yet.

panels.title: Captioning app
panels.description: UP/DOWN of the app's /metrics endpoint (port 28000). Blue = up, orange-red = down; text label also shown.

panels.title: Node exporter
panels.description: UP/DOWN of node_exporter (port 9100), the source of host CPU/RAM/disk data.

panels.title: Model loaded
panels.description: 1 once the BLIP model is resident in memory.

panels.title: Model load time
panels.description: Seconds the app took to load BLIP at start-up (gauge caption_model_load_seconds). Cold start cost.

panels.title: Active requests
panels.description: Requests currently being served (single + bulk). Spikes mean the CPU is busy.

panels.title: Success ratio (5 m)
panels.description: Share of images captioned without error over the last 5 minutes. 'No data' = no traffic in that window.

panels.title: Last request
panels.description: Time since the last user request (gauge caption_last_request_timestamp_seconds). Large = app idle; No data = no request since start.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Number of Prometheus alerts currently firing (rules in alert_rules.yml). Details in the table at the bottom.

panels.title: 2 · Throughput — how much work is done?

options.content: **The story:** Single (solid) is occasional; Bulk (dashed) arrives in bursts of images per second. The Errors panel stays empty while the app is healthy.

panels.title: Throughput · images per second
panels.description: Images captioned per second, split by Single vs Bulk mode (1-minute rate). Bulk bursts dominate. Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: Requests · by mode
panels.description: User requests (button clicks) per minute for each mode; one bulk request contains many images. Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: Errors · by type
panels.description: Errors per minute by type (bad image, bad zip, inference, size limit). Flat at zero is healthy. Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: 3 · Latency — how long does each image take?

options.content: **The story:** on a CPU one image takes seconds, not milliseconds. The gap between p50 and p99 shows the slow tail; the HighInferenceLatencyP95 alert fires when p95 passes 10 s.

panels.title: Inference latency · percentiles (log scale)
panels.description: p50 / p95 / p99 model inference time per image, all modes (1-minute window). Log₂ axis so tails stay visible. Y-axis scale: log.

panels.title: Mean inference time · by mode
panels.description: Average seconds per image computed from the histogram _sum/_count, Single vs Bulk. Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: Request latency p95 · end to end
panels.description: 95th-percentile wall time of a whole request (upload→result). Bulk is much longer than Single by design. Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: 4 · Payload & pipeline — what goes in, where the time goes

options.content: **The story:** model inference is about 100× slower than decoding and resizing (log axis), so the CPU-bound model, not I/O, is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Pipeline stages · preprocess vs inference
panels.description: Mean seconds per image spent decoding/resizing vs running BLIP (histogram _sum/_count). Inference dominates by ~100×, hence the log₂ axis. Y-axis scale: log.

panels.title: Caption length · words (Summary)
panels.description: Mean words per generated caption, Single vs Bulk, from the Summary's _sum/_count. A sudden drop would hint at degenerate output. Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: Upload payload · image size and bandwidth
panels.description: Left: mean uploaded image size (Summary caption_image_size_bytes). Right: upload bandwidth from the caption_upload_bytes_total counter. Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: Bulk jobs · batch size, ZIP size, skipped entries
panels.description: Mean images per bulk request (histogram) and mean ZIP size (Summary), plus ZIP entries skipped per 5 min (dirs, non-images, over limit). 5-minute window because bulk jobs are rare. Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: 5 · System resources — what does the hardware feel?

options.content: **The story:** host CPU and app CPU (both as % of all cores) rise together during inference; app memory steps up once when the model loads and then stays flat.

panels.title: Host CPU · utilisation
panels.description: Whole-machine CPU busy % from node_exporter vs. the app process alone, both as a share of all cores so they are comparable. Right: app thread count (torch spawns workers during inference). Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: Memory · host and app
panels.description: Host RAM in use (%, left) vs. app resident memory (GiB, right axis). Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: Disk · usage and I/O
panels.description: Root disk used % (left) and host disk write rate (right, bytes/s). Model/ZIP temp files show up as write bursts. Y-axis scale: linear.

options.content: **The story:** when a bulk job starts, “images remaining” jumps to N; host CPU climbs and stays high until it counts down to 0, and the load average follows. This is the app-to-hardware link.

panels.title: Bulk upload vs host CPU
panels.description: Left: host CPU %. Right: images remaining in the active bulk job. CPU climbs when a bulk job starts and falls as the backlog drains. Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: Throughput vs CPU load
panels.description: Left: images/s processed. Right: 1-minute load average. Throughput plateaus once CPU saturates — more load only raises latency. Y-axis scale: linear.

panels.title: 7 · Who is using it, what is running, what is wrong? (metadata)

options.content: **The story:** who is sending the load (session and source IP), which alerts are firing right now, and which model and device are serving requests.

panels.title: Top clients · images processed (since app start)
panels.description: Images captioned per session id / source IP, Single vs Bulk, from the counter's current value (cumulative since the app started). Shows who drives the load.

panels.title: Firing alerts · details
panels.description: Alerts currently firing in Prometheus (alert_rules.yml), also routed to Alertmanager on :9093. Empty = healthy.

panels.title: Running model · app info
panels.description: Static build info from the Info metric caption_app_info: which model, framework and device serve requests.
